# Deckard 1.12.0 - Word Compare, Folder Compare, shareable reports, and formatting comparison

Deckard now has eight tools. **Word Compare** and **Folder Compare** are new, Text, Image, Excel, PDF and Folder Compare can write a report you can send to someone, and Excel, Word and PDF Compare now notice when the same content *looks* different.

## What is new

- **Formatting comparison.** Excel, Word and PDF Compare now compare how things look as well as what they say, and it is **on by default**.
  - **Excel:** number format, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, font, size, colour, fill and the four borders of each cell. A cell with the same value but a different look is shown in light blue; a changed value that also changed look lists both.
  - **PDF:** the font, size, colour, bold and italic of words that are in both PDFs, listed with the page and the words, for example `"Total due": bold: no to yes`. The window has a **Compare formatting** box and a blue list above the text in Code view; the report has a Formatting differences column and a section for each page.
  - **Word:** see below.
  - On the command line it is `compareFormatting` on `excel`, `word`, `pdf` and `folder`; set it to false to ignore how things look.
- **Word Compare.** Drop two `.docx` (or `.docm`) documents and Deckard compares them paragraph by paragraph: the body, tables, text boxes, headers, footers, footnotes, endnotes and comments, each as its own part. Changed words are marked. A paragraph with the same words but a different look (bold, italic, underline, font, size, colour, highlight, paragraph style, alignment, indent, list level, table cell shading) is listed as a formatting change, with the words that differ. **Tracked changes** are listed for each document, and a tracked change that is in only one of them counts as a difference. The text compared is what a reader sees with tracked changes accepted. On the command line it is `Deckard.Cli.exe word request.json`, and the MCP server offers it as a tool.
- **Folder Compare.** Pick two folders and Deckard pairs the files by name and compares each pair with the right tool: text, Excel, Word, image or PDF; any other file is compared byte for byte. Files that are the same are skipped quickly, a file that cannot be compared counts as a difference, and **Open comparison** (or a double click) opens that pair in its own window. Its report is a summary plus a folder holding each differing file's own report. On the command line it is `folder`.
- **Reports you can share.** Text, Image, Excel, PDF and Folder Compare have an **Export report...** button that saves a summary, pie charts and the differences as a **PDF**, a **web page** (one self-contained file) or both. From a script, add `report` and `outputFolder` to any request. The PDF is drawn by Deckard itself, so it needs no browser, and stays small (a few hundred KB).
- **A way to fail a build.** `Deckard.exe site compare --fail-on-differences` and `"failOnDifferences": true` for Data Compare now exit with code 3 when there are differences (the reports are still written); `text`, `excel`, `word`, `pdf`, `image` and `folder` already did.

## Things to know

- **Formatting comparison is on by default, so pairs that used to match can now show differences.** A file that only differs in how it looks, such as a header made bold or a figure turned red, is now a difference. Untick **Compare formatting**, or set `compareFormatting` to false, to get the old behaviour.
- **Limits of formatting comparison.**
  - *PDF:* bold and italic are worked out from the font's flags and name, so a bold font that never says so is read as not bold; a scanned page has no text to read; pages are matched by position; text that moved counts as a layout change. The plain `report.txt` from the `pdf` command does not list formatting.
  - *Word:* table styles, style toggle rules and conditional formatting are not resolved; a theme colour is named, not turned into its RGB; paragraphs with no text are ignored; text inside pictures is not read; moved text shows as removed plus added; old `.doc` files are refused with a message.
  - *Excel:* a theme colour is named, not resolved, so two themes that look different can compare equal.
- **Folder Compare and PDFs.** A pair of PDFs is also compared as pictures, so a formatting-only change shows even with **Compare formatting** off.
- **Not yet tried on real-world files.** Formatting comparison was checked on generated documents; PDFs with embedded subset fonts and Word contracts with numbering, fields and content controls are the likeliest places to find something unexpected.
